# mulib-audio-device

<!-- Generated by tools/media_inventory.py; edit CONTRACTS or section-7 scope, then --write-docs. -->

**Area:** Audio  
**Implementation:** C11 `static inline`; no implementation switch or external ABI export  
**Status:** bounded review candidate; **not safe On1x admitted**

## Purpose and limits

Audio provider lifecycle and partial-frame writes.

No native device provider; bridge existing miniaudio or platform audio.

Retain existing upstream functionality and platform providers; this header is not a replacement for a complete media/editor/rendering stack.

## Units, ownership and capacities

Provider write takes frames n, not floats; storage covers n*device.channels floats. written reports partial frames. Start/stop/close lifecycle is provider-owned; no native device is bundled.

PCM is interleaved float unless stated otherwise. A frame has one sample per channel; frames*channels counts floats, not bytes. Rate and frequency are Hz; times are seconds where used for attack/release. Inputs, states and scratch are caller-owned. Supply finite samples/parameters. Initialize state outside realtime callbacks; avoid allocation, blocking, disk I/O and ordinary locks on the realtime thread.

Capacities describe live backing storage supplied by the caller, not merely numeric metadata. Check return values before using outputs. A false result is not a universal no-mutation guarantee; low-level value helpers and bool miss/error results require the documented preconditions. Bound untrusted counts and work before calling.

## Current callable surface

Signatures extracted from this header; dependency types and complete checks are in [the source](../include/mulib-audio-device.h). Helpers listed here are not automatically safe foreign imports.

```c
static inline bool mulib_audio_device_valid(const mulib_audio_device *d);
static inline mulib_media_status mulib_audio_device_status(mulib_media_status s);
static inline mulib_media_status mulib_audio_device_start(mulib_audio_device *d);
static inline mulib_media_status mulib_audio_device_write(mulib_audio_device *d,const float *p,size_t n,size_t *written);
static inline mulib_media_status mulib_audio_device_stop(mulib_audio_device *d);
static inline void mulib_audio_device_close(mulib_audio_device *d);
```

## Additional source contracts

- Provider owns the real device, thread affinity and blocking policy; calls below are control/output operations, NOT realtime-callback-safe guarantees. No native device is opened here. Context is move-only/caller-serialized. PCM limits match mulib-audio.h. Provider must not retain borrowed samples.
- n/written count FRAMES. p has n*channels finite floats, disjoint from d and written. A provider may report partial progress even on error; impossible progress is replaced by zero/IO. Validation failure changes nothing.

## Validation and integration

The [shared CPU example](../examples/media-pipeline.c) illustrates a small image/audio/timebase slice; it does **not** exercise every API in this header. The [integration oracles](../tests/media-integration-test.c) and [parser boundary probes](../tests/media-parser-boundary-test.c) are representative regressions, not exhaustive coverage.

```sh
python3 tools/check_media.py
```

The runner checks the 193 original kernels plus the shared PCM helper, isolated and in aggregate C11 builds with GCC/Clang, including canonical-header composition, separate-TU wrappers, an expected missing-static-inline-export link failure, a no-`__int128` path, and ASan/UBSan regressions. It does not validate native GPU/codec/audio execution, real-world compatibility, C++ or On1x ownership/admission. Explicit foreign wrappers, independent safety review and platform integration are still required.
